note.question: How can a search platform recover advertisers' private values from quality-weighted GSP bids and choose ad-quality scoring rules to improve revenue?
note.overview: Advertisers with private values and ad qualities strategically shade bids in a weighted generalized-second-price auction. The paper proves and uses a unique symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium to identify valuations and evaluate platform quality-scoring rules.

coverage.note: The existing independently audited model map was decomposed into Mini-style components and linked back to the page-preserving source extraction.

models.name: Incomplete-information weighted GSP auction with equilibrium-based nonparametric identification of advertiser values

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: For a search opportunity, advertisers observe their private values and ad qualities and simultaneously submit bids. The platform ranks weighted bids, assigns ordered positions and charges each winner the minimum per-click price needed to retain its rank. Clicks and profits are then realized. Ranking depends on both strategic bids and platform-generated ad-quality weights.

components.label: Unique symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium of the weighted generalized-second-price auction
components.explanation: The model's equilibrium concept is Unique symmetric Bayesian Nash equilibrium of the weighted generalized-second-price auction. Assumptions 1 and 2 establish the incomplete-information and monotonicity environment. Theorem 1 reduces equilibrium weighted bids to a function of weighted value, and Lemma 1 gives the unique symmetric Bayesian Nash bidding strategy used for identification.
